purpose: Run a Termux-owned outbound polling agent that reports compact health and receives allowlisted bounded commands from a central fleet controller.
authority_boundary: Termux remains a normal Android app sidecar.
The fleet agent does not create ADB authorization, become Android shell, replace HOME, own broker authority, or act as a hidden watchdog.
Local ADB commands are allowed only when an already authorized Wi-Fi ADB endpoint is available and the command explicitly requires it.
The first implementation uses outbound polling and exposes no inbound listener on the headset.

preflight.label: agent-config
preflight.command: Review the public-safe agent config and confirm fleet_id, agent_id, central endpoint, command allowlist, and local ADB setting.

preflight.label: central-controller
preflight.command: Start the central fleet controller on a controlled lab host or simulator.

preflight.label: termux-runtime
preflight.command: Confirm Termux can run Python 3 and write to the agent workspace.

start.label: queue-command
start.command: Queue an agent.status command through the central controller.

start.label: queue-verified-update
start.command: Queue an apk.update_verified command with a package/version/hash/signing-digest/rollout-ring manifest and requires_local_adb_shell=true.

status.label: heartbeat
status.command: Confirm the central controller has a fresh heartbeat for the agent.

status.label: command-result
status.command: Confirm the central controller received a bounded command result with matching command_id and agent_id.

status.label: local-evidence
status.command: Confirm the agent wrote local JSONL command/result evidence under its workspace.

stop.label: stop-agent
stop.command: Stop the foreground agent process or write a reviewed stop condition for a bounded test run.

cleanup.label: no-listener
cleanup.command: Confirm the outbound-only agent did not leave an inbound listener.

cleanup.label: redaction
cleanup.command: Keep real fleet logs, device names, IPs, package IDs, and ADB outputs out of the public repository.

evidence: Verified APK update result records with idempotency, update report, rollback report, and recovery action.
ADB shell lease state when local ADB is checked.

risks.risk: Android may pause or kill long-running Termux processes.
risks.recovery: Treat stale heartbeat as recovery-needed and use central direct ADB or operator action to restore the agent.

risks.risk: Wi-Fi ADB may be unavailable even when the agent is alive.
risks.recovery: Reject commands that require local ADB and escalate to central direct ADB only when needed.

risks.risk: An overly broad command allowlist can become remote shell control.
risks.recovery: Keep command kinds explicit, bounded, and logged; reject arbitrary shell by default.

risks.risk: Verified APK updates can fail safely when the ADB lease is missing.
risks.recovery: Report central_direct_adb_recovery and let the live Quest operations layer restore or validate ADB.

notes: This recipe is for fleet monitoring and bounded control, not live device validation by itself.
The synthetic examples intentionally do not contain real headset names, serials, LAN IPs, or authorization material.
